name: WaterfallChart
intent: How a balance got from one total to another: an opening total, the rises and falls that moved it, and the closing total.
usage: Use WaterfallChart to explain a change, like an account balance from last month's close to this month's: opening balance, new charges, credits, payments, closing balance. It is one component: pass items, one per bar, in the order they happened. A change moves the running total by its value, up or down; an item with kind "total" draws from zero at its value, for the opening and closing bars. Each bar starts where the one before it ended, and a thin dotted line joins them. Colours come from direction: riseIntent for up, fallIntent for down, totalIntent for the totals; a single item can name its own intent. Values are written over each bar with their sign, so a fall reads as a fall without its colour. Hover or use the arrow keys for a tooltip with the change and the running total. See contracts/waterfallchart.json for the full contract.

label.note: Names the chart for screen readers and captions its data table, like Balance movement this month.

title.note: Visible title over the chart. The screen-reader name still comes from label.

subtitle.note: A quieter line under the title, like Northwind Traders, September.

showHeader.note: Turns the title and subtitle off when the Card or Section around the chart already says the same.

items.itemShape: { label: string; value: number; kind?: "change" | "total"; intent?: ChartIntent }
items.note: One entry per bar, in the order they happened. A change (the default) moves the running total by value, which may be negative. kind "total" draws a bar from zero at value, for an opening or closing balance. intent overrides the colour the bar takes from its direction.

riseIntent.note: The colour of a change that goes up.

fallIntent.note: The colour of a change that goes down. Pick the pair that fits the measure: on a balance a fall is good news, so it is not red by default.

totalIntent.note: The colour of the opening and closing bars, which are not a change.

showValues.note: Writes each bar's value over it, short and signed (−$340K). Turn it off only when the tooltip is enough.

showConnectors.note: The thin dotted line from one bar's end to the next bar's start, which is what makes it read as one running total.

showGrid.note: Faint lines across the chart at the ticks.

showLegend.note: A key for up, down and total. Off by default: the signed values already say which is which.

animate.note: Grows the bars in on first paint. Never plays when the person prefers reduced motion.

format.note: How values read. Axis ticks and bar labels are short; the tooltip and table show the full number.

currency.note: The currency code for format currency.

height.note: Height of the drawing in px, axis labels included. The width fills the container.

emptyLabel.note: What the chart says in place of the drawing when there is nothing to draw.

useWhen: A balance from its opening to its closing total, with the charges, credits and payments between.
Revenue from last period to this one, broken into new, expansion, contraction and churn.
An invoice total built up from its line items, with the total bar at the end.
doNot: Do not use it for a trend over time. Every bar here is a step in one sum, not a period: use LineChart or BarChart.
Do not use it for parts of a total that do not run in an order. Use PieChart or a stacked BarChart.
Do not leave the opening and closing bars out. Without them the rises and falls float, and the chart says nothing.
Do not make a fall red by default. On a balance a fall is good news; pick the pair that fits the measure.
Do not turn showConnectors off to tidy the chart. The line is what makes the bars one running total.
Do not draw charts with loose SVG or a chart library. Use the kit charts.
Do not use raw hex; pick an intent.
a11y: A figure named by label. The drawing is hidden from screen readers; a visually hidden table holds every bar, with its change and the running total after it.
Totals are named as totals in the table, so a reader can tell the opening and closing bars from the changes.
The chart takes focus: the arrow keys (and Home and End) move through the bars and show the same tooltip as pointing at them. Escape hides it.
Values are written over the bars with their sign, so direction never rests on colour alone.
Motion is subtle and optional (animate), and never plays when the person prefers reduced motion.
snippet:
<WaterfallChart
  label="Balance movement this month"
  items={[
    { label: "Opening", value: 482000, kind: "total" },
    { label: "New charges", value: 196000 },
    { label: "Credits", value: -42000 },
    { label: "Payments", value: -318000 },
    { label: "Closing", value: 318000, kind: "total" },
  ]}
  format="currency"
/>
